definition_zh: 熟练程度；精通；语言水平
definition_en: a high level of skill or command in a subject or activity, especially in a language
core_image: 一位口译员在隔间里边听边译，耳机旁摆着一份评分表
scene: 一位译员在隔间里边听边译，术语与语速都没能拖住他。 Her proficiency in two languages won her the post.
sceneCN: 译员在隔间里边听边译，术语与语速都没拖住她；句中的 proficiency 指「语言上达到的高水平运用能力」（第 1 个义项：对语言的熟练掌控）。图中可辨识物件：隔间、耳机、评分表、术语本。

pos.zh: 熟练程度；精通；（语言的）水平

senses.title: Command of a language
senses.definition: the ability to use a language accurately and fluently for real purposes
senses.definitionCN: 为实际目的准确而流畅地使用一种语言的能力
senses.example: Her proficiency in two languages won her the post.
senses.exampleCN: 她两种语言都熟练，因此赢得了这个职位。
senses.why: proficere meant 'to make progress', so proficiency measures how far someone has advanced in a skill rather than how long they have studied it.
senses.whyCN: proficere 意为「取得进展」，因此 proficiency 衡量的是一个人在技能上走到多远，而非学了多久。

senses.title: High skill in a field
senses.titleCN: 某一领域的高水平技能
senses.definition: a strong working command of a subject such as law, music or surgery
senses.definitionCN: 在法律、音乐或外科等领域具备扎实的实操能力
senses.example: The post requires proficiency in statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 这个职位要求统计方面的熟练能力。
senses.why: the word moved from language to any practised field, because every field has a level at which a person can work unaided.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从语言扩展到任何需要练习的领域，因为每个领域都有一个人可以独立工作的水平线。

senses.title: A measured level on a scale
senses.titleCN: 按等级量表测出的水平
senses.definition: a score or band that places a learner at a defined stage
senses.definitionCN: 把学习者放入某个明确阶段的分数或等级
senses.example: She reached the upper proficiency band after one year.
senses.exampleCN: 一年后她达到了较高的水平等级。
senses.why: testing turned advancement into a rung: once a scale exists, proficiency can be reported as a band rather than a vague compliment.
senses.whyCN: 测试把「进展」变成一级台阶：量表一旦存在，水平就能报成一个等级，而不只是模糊的称赞。

senses.title: Mastery gained by practice
senses.definition: the fluency that comes from repeated use rather than from native origin
senses.definitionCN: 由反复使用而非母语出身带来的流畅
senses.example: His proficiency came from years of night shifts in the emergency room.
senses.exampleCN: 他的熟练来自急诊室里多年的夜班。
senses.why: because proficiency is progress, it belongs to learners: a native speaker has a language, but proficiency is what practice earns.
senses.whyCN: 因为 proficiency 是「进展」，它属于学习者：母语者拥有一种语言，而熟练是练习挣来的。

senses.title: A professional standard
senses.definition: the level a profession sets before someone may practise independently
senses.definitionCN: 行业规定的、可以独立执业前必须达到的水平
senses.example: The board checks proficiency before issuing a licence.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在发执照前核查专业能力。
senses.why: professions need a threshold, and proficiency supplies the neutral word for it without claiming excellence.
senses.whyCN: 行业需要一个门槛，proficiency 正好提供这个中性词，而不宣称卓越。

senses.title: Operational skill with tools
senses.titleCN: 使用工具与仪器的熟练
senses.definition: the practised ability to handle an instrument or a technique
senses.definitionCN: 操作仪器或运用技法的熟练能力
senses.example: The technician showed proficiency with the laser cutter.
senses.exampleCN: 这位技师表现出使用激光切割机的熟练度。
senses.why: skill with a tool is progress made visible in the hands, which is why the word fits craft and laboratory work.
senses.whyCN: 使用工具的技艺是显现在手上的进展，因此这个词也适合手艺与实验工作。

senses.title: A limited degree of skill
senses.definition: a modest working ability, enough for simple tasks but not for complex ones
senses.definitionCN: 足以应付简单任务、不足以应付复杂任务的有限能力
senses.example: The form asks applicants to state their proficiency in each language.
senses.exampleCN: 表格要求申请人写明每种语言的熟练程度。
senses.why: proficiency is gradable, so a form can ask for it without implying mastery; the scale runs from limited to full.
senses.whyCN: proficiency 可分等级，因此表格可以询问它而不暗示精通；量表从有限到完全都能排。

senses.title: A certified level for study
senses.titleCN: 为求学或工作认证的水平
senses.definition: an officially recorded level accepted by a university or an employer
senses.definitionCN: 被大学或雇主接受的、正式记录在案的水平
senses.example: The university accepts a proficiency certificate instead of an entrance test.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学接受水平证书以替代入学测试。
senses.why: institutions need portable evidence, so proficiency became something a certificate can carry between countries.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要可携带的证据，于是 proficiency 变成一张能在国家之间携带的证书。

intro.en: Proficiency is proficient plus -ency. Proficient comes from Latin proficere 'to make progress, accomplish', built on pro- 'forward' and facere 'to do, make'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: proficiency 由 proficient 加名词后缀构成。proficient 来自拉丁 proficere「取得进展、完成」，由 pro-「向前」与 facere「做、造」构成。年代为约数。

items.en: Facere meant 'to do, make, bring about'. It is one of the most productive roots in English, giving fact, effect, office and dozens of verbs in -fic.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造、促成」，是英语中产量最高的词根之一，给出 fact、effect、office 以及大量由它构成的动词。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus facere produced proficere 'to make progress, to accomplish, to be useful'. The forward prefix is what separates it from plain doing.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 facere 构成 proficere「取得进展、完成、有用」。这个向前的方向正是它与单纯「做」的区别。

items.en: The present participle proficiens 'making progress, effective' described a person or thing that gets somewhere.
items.cn: 现在分词 proficiens「有进展的、有效的」用于描述能走到某处的人或物。

items.en: English took proficient in the sixteenth century, first as 'useful, advantageous' and soon as 'well advanced in a skill'.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收 proficient，最初意为「有用的、有利的」，很快转为「在技能上进展良好的」。

items.en: The noun proficiency appeared in the seventeenth century as the state of being proficient; modern testing fixed it to measured language levels in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 名词 proficiency 于十七世纪出现，指熟练的状态；现代测试在二十世纪把它固定为可测量的语言等级。

items.en: The deeper origin of facere is generally connected to a root meaning 'to put, set', but the exact chain is reconstructed. The early history of the English -ency noun is also thinly documented.
items.cn: facere 的更早来源一般被认为与表示「放置」的词根相关，但确切链条属重构。英语中这个表状态名词的早期历史记录也较单薄。

note.en: Group one holds the same Latin root under different prefixes and a look-alike that means something else; group two holds words for skill, each with a different centre of gravity.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词根但前缀不同的词，以及一个形似而义异的词；第二组是表示技能的词，重心各不相同。

entries.definition: The adjective describing the person; proficiency is the noun for the level itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述人的形容词；proficiency 是表示水平本身的名词。

entries.definition: From ex- 'out' plus facere: producing a result with little waste, a different idea from being well advanced.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ex-「出」加 facere：以很少耗费产出结果，与「进展良好」不是同一概念。

entries.definition: From sub- 'under' plus facere: enough to meet a need, which is a matter of quantity, not skill.
entries.definitionCN: 由 sub-「在下」加 facere：足以满足需要，关乎数量而非技能。

entries.definition: Looks close and shares the forward prefix, but comes through French for 'advantage gained', not from the participle of proficere.
entries.definitionCN: 形近且同有向前的前缀，但经法语指「所得利益」，并非来自 proficere 的分词。

entries.definition: The ease and speed of speech; proficiency also covers accuracy and range, not only smoothness.
entries.definitionCN: 指说话的轻松与速度；proficiency 还涵盖准确度与覆盖面，不只是顺滑。

entries.definition: A higher claim than proficiency: complete control of a field, not merely a working level.
entries.definitionCN: 比 proficiency 更强的说法：对某一领域的完全掌控，而非仅有工作水平。

entries.definition: The threshold of being able to act; proficiency usually implies a level above that threshold.
entries.definitionCN: 指足以行动的门槛；proficiency 通常意味着高于该门槛的水平。

entries.definition: Deep specialist knowledge, often recognized by others; proficiency can be self-measured.
entries.definitionCN: 指深的专门知识，常由他人认可；proficiency 则可由自己测出。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the real Latin steps, the real prefix contrast and the real settings where the noun is used.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自真实的拉丁演变、真实的前缀对照，以及这个名词真实的使用场合。

normal.en: pro- 'forward' plus facere 'do': to be moving forward in what one does.
normal.cn: pro-「向前」加 facere「做」：在做的事上不断向前。

normal.en: The same root gives efficient with ex-, sufficient with sub-, and proficiency with pro-.
normal.cn: 同一词根配 ex- 得 efficient，配 sub- 得 sufficient，配 pro- 得 proficiency。

normal.en: The noun is gradable: limited proficiency, working proficiency, full proficiency.
normal.cn: 这个名词可分等级：有限熟练、工作熟练、完全熟练。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark testing: proficiency test, proficiency level, language proficiency.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出测试场景：水平测试、熟练等级、语言水平。

normal.en: The word belongs to learners, not to native origin: practice produces it.
normal.cn: 这个词属于学习者，而不属于母语出身：练习才产出它。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder standing in a language classroom, each rung labelled with what a learner can now do.
abstract.cn: 想象语言教室里立着一把梯子，每一级都标着学习者现在能做的事。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of headphones still warm from hours of practice.
abstract.cn: 想象一副耳机还带着数小时练习的余温。

abstract.en: Picture a certificate that travels in a pocket from one country to another.
abstract.cn: 想象一张证书被装进口袋，从一个国家带到另一个国家。

examples.en: Applicants must show proficiency in written English.
examples.cn: 申请人必须证明书面英语熟练。

examples.en: Her proficiency with the instrument surprised the orchestra.
examples.cn: 她对这件乐器的熟练让乐团吃了一惊。

examples.en: The course takes students from beginner to working proficiency.
examples.cn: 这门课把学生从初学带到工作水平。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pro（向前）+ fic（做）」——一直向前做，越做越熟 → 熟练、水平

root: 拉丁 pro-「向前」+ facere「做」→ proficere「取得进展、完成」→ 分词 proficiens → 英语 proficient 加名词后缀 → proficiency；facere 的更早来源一般与「放置」词根相关，确切链条属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one ladder: a learner moves forward in a skill, the moving shows as command of a language, then as skill in any field, as a band on a scale, as the fruit of practice, as a professional threshold, as tool craft, as a limited degree and finally as portable certified evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一把梯子展开：学习者在技能上向前走，这份前进先表现为语言掌控，再表现为各领域的技能、量表上的等级、练习的果实、职业门槛、工具手艺、有限的程度，最后成为可携带的认证证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ladder whose rungs are labelled with what a learner can do, and the climb is measured rather than merely praised.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把梯子，每级标着学习者能做的事，而攀爬是被测量的，不只是被称赞。

branches.en: COMMAND: the same forward movement shows first in a language, then in any practised field.
branches.cn: 掌控：同一份向前的进展先显于语言，再显于任何经过练习的领域。

branches.en: SCALE: a measured band and a limited degree are two readings of the same ruler.
branches.cn: 量表：测出的等级与有限的程度，是同一把尺子的两种读数。

branches.en: PRACTICE: the climb belongs to learners, because practice is what produces it.
branches.cn: 练习：这段攀爬属于学习者，因为产出它的是练习。

branches.en: THRESHOLD AND TOOL: a profession sets a rung, and a craft shows the rung in the hands.
branches.cn: 门槛与工具：行业设下一级，手艺把这一级显在手上。

branches.en: PORTABLE PROOF: what was climbed becomes a paper that crosses borders.
branches.cn: 可携带的证明：爬到的位置变成一张能跨越国界的纸。

intro.en: The noun is a Latin prefix and root plus an English suffix, and the same pieces build a large family of English words.
intro.cn: 这个名词由拉丁前缀、词根加一个英语后缀构成，同一批部件还造出一大族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Pro- and facere build proficere, whose participle gives proficient; the English suffix -ency turns the adjective into a noun of state.
latinIntro.cn: pro- 与 facere 构成 proficere，其分词给出 proficient；英语中的名词后缀把形容词变成表状态的名词。

definition_zh: n. 可能发生的意外；应急方案；偶然性
definition_en: a possible future event, or a plan for one
core_image: 抽屉里备着一只手电筒，等停电时用
scene: 预算里留出一成资金，用来应付意外。 The plan keeps a tenth of the budget for contingencies.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：contingency 指可能发生的意外；句意是预算留钱应付意外。

pos.zh: 意外情况；应急方案；偶然性

senses.title: A possible event
senses.definition: something that may happen but is not certain
senses.definitionCN: 可能发生但不确定的事
senses.example: Bad weather is a contingency we must plan for.
senses.exampleCN: 坏天气是我们必须准备的意外。
senses.why: A branch on a path that may be taken.
senses.whyCN: 路上可能走的一条岔路。

senses.title: A backup plan
senses.definition: arrangements made in case something happens
senses.definitionCN: 为防万一而做的安排
senses.example: The team drew up a contingency.
senses.exampleCN: 团队拟好了一套应急方案。
senses.why: A spare key kept in a drawer.
senses.whyCN: 抽屉里备着的一把钥匙。

senses.title: Dependence on chance
senses.definition: the state of depending on chance
senses.definitionCN: 依赖机缘的状态
senses.example: The outcome has too much contingency.
senses.exampleCN: 结果太依赖偶然因素。
senses.why: Dice decide nothing in advance.
senses.whyCN: 骰子从不预先决定结果。

senses.title: An unforeseen cost
senses.definition: an extra expense no one predicted
senses.definitionCN: 没人预料到的额外支出
senses.example: A repair fund covers contingencies.
senses.exampleCN: 维修基金用来支付意外开支。
senses.why: A hole in the road costs money.
senses.whyCN: 路上的坑也要花钱。

intro.en: Contingency comes from Latin contingere, to happen or touch.
intro.cn: contingency 来自拉丁语 contingere，意为发生、触及。

items.en: Tangere means to touch.
items.cn: tangere 意为触摸。

items.en: Contingere means to happen, to fall to one.
items.cn: contingere 意为发生、落到某人身上。

items.en: Contingentia names what may happen.
items.cn: contingentia 指可能发生之事。

items.en: English used contingency for chance events.

items.en: Insurance sold cover for contingencies.

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the conting- stem; the near-meaning group names things that might happen.

definition_zh: 再生；更新；（森林）天然更新；复兴
definition_en: the regrowth of lost tissue or vegetation, and more broadly the renewal of a system or a place
core_image: 被截断的蚯蚓尾端一点点长出新的体节，断口边缘先是一层薄薄的新肉
scene: 砍伐后的山坡先铺满苔藓与草本，随后成片冒起桦树苗，十年后又是一片幼林。 On the cleared slope, natural regeneration began with moss and grass and ended with a young birch wood.
sceneCN: 这里 regeneration 指「植被天然更新」（第 2 个义项：森林在受扰后自行重新长出新一代林木）；句意：在清伐后的坡地上，天然更新从苔藓与草本开始，最后长成一片幼桦林。图中可辨识物件：苔藓层、草本、桦树苗、幼林轮廓。

pos.zh: 再生；更新；复兴（可数或不可数，复数为 regenerations）

senses.title: Biological regrowth of lost tissue
senses.titleCN: 组织再生：长回失去的部分
senses.definition: the regrowth of cells, tissue or a body part that has been lost or damaged
senses.definitionCN: 细胞、组织或身体部件在失去或受损后重新长出
senses.example: Lizard tail regeneration takes several months.
senses.exampleCN: 蜥蜴尾巴的再生需要数月。
senses.why: re- 'again' plus generare 'to beget' names a second birth of the same part.
senses.whyCN: re-「再一次」加 generare「生育」，指同一部位获得第二次生长。

senses.title: Renewal of forest or vegetation
senses.titleCN: 植被更新：新一代林木长起
senses.definition: the establishment of a new generation of trees or plants after harvesting or disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 在采伐或扰动之后新一代树木或植物建立起来
senses.example: Natural regeneration depends on seed trees left standing.
senses.exampleCN: 天然更新依赖留存的母树。
senses.why: forestry applies the same 'new generation' idea to a stand rather than to a single tissue.
senses.whyCN: 林学把同一个「新一代」的概念从单个组织扩展到整片林分。

senses.title: Spiritual rebirth
senses.titleCN: 灵魂重生：宗教意义上的更新
senses.definition: a renewal of the soul or of a person's moral life, especially in Christian usage
senses.definitionCN: 灵魂或道德生活的更新，尤见于基督教用语
senses.example: The sermon described baptism as a regeneration of the spirit.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇讲道把洗礼描述为灵魂的重生。
senses.why: the earliest English sense is theological: a new life given from outside the person.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的含义是神学的：从人之外赐予的新生命。

senses.title: Urban or economic renewal
senses.definition: the revival of a declining district or economy through investment and rebuilding
senses.definitionCN: 通过投资与重建使衰退城区或经济复苏
senses.example: The docklands regeneration brought new housing and jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 码头区的更新带来了新住房与就业。
senses.why: a district is treated as a body that can grow a new layer over its old fabric.
senses.whyCN: 城区被当成一个身体，能在旧结构上长出新的一层。

senses.title: Restoring a system's capacity
senses.titleCN: 系统能力恢复：功能重新运转
senses.definition: the restoration of a system's ability to function after decline or damage
senses.definitionCN: 系统在衰退或受损后恢复运作能力
senses.example: The regeneration of the soil's microbial community took years.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤微生物群落的恢复花了数年。
senses.why: the sense focuses on capacity rather than on the visible parts, so it applies to soil, reefs or institutions.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项着眼能力而非可见部件，因此可用于土壤、礁体或机构。

senses.title: Rebuilding a population
senses.titleCN: 种群重建：个体数量回升
senses.definition: the recovery of a population through reproduction after a decline
senses.definitionCN: 种群在数量下降后通过繁殖回升
senses.example: Wolf regeneration in the park followed a ban on hunting.
senses.exampleCN: 禁猎之后，公园里的狼群得以重建。
senses.why: when the unit is a breeding group rather than a body part, 'new generation' becomes population growth.
senses.whyCN: 当单位是繁殖群体而非身体部件时，「新一代」就变成种群增长。

senses.title: Industrial regeneration of materials
senses.titleCN: 工业再生：材料与介质复原
senses.definition: the restoration of a spent material or medium so that it can be used again
senses.definitionCN: 使用过的材料或介质恢复可用状态
senses.example: Catalyst regeneration cut the refinery's costs.
senses.exampleCN: 催化剂再生降低了炼厂成本。
senses.why: industry reuses the biological word for a technical second life of a material.
senses.whyCN: 工业借用了生物学的词，指材料在技术上获得的第二次寿命。

senses.title: Literary renewal of memory or ideas
senses.titleCN: 文学义：记忆与观念的复苏
senses.definition: the revival of a memory, idea or tradition that had faded
senses.definitionCN: 已淡去的记忆、观念或传统重新活跃
senses.example: The festival led to a regeneration of the old dialect.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日带来了古老方言的复苏。
senses.why: the least physical branch: what returns is not tissue but a pattern of thought or speech.
senses.whyCN: 最不具实体的一支：回来的不是组织，而是一套思想或言语模式。

intro.en: Regeneration comes from Latin regeneratio, built on regenerare 'to bring forth again', itself re- plus generare 'to beget' from genus 'birth, race'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: regeneration 出自拉丁 regeneratio，基于 regenerare「再次产生」，后者由 re- 加 generare「生育」构成，而 generare 源自 genus「出生、族类」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Genus meant 'birth, origin, race, kind'; its stem gener- carries the idea of a line coming into being.
items.cn: genus 意为「出生、来源、族类、种类」；其词干 gener- 承载「一条血脉产生出来」的意思。

items.en: Generare 'to beget, produce' gave English generate and generation; it names bringing a new instance into existence.
items.cn: generare「生育、产生」衍生英语 generate 与 generation；它指使一个新个体进入存在。

items.en: Re- 'again' plus generare produced regenerare 'to bring forth again', used of both living things and spiritual renewal.
items.cn: re-「再一次」加 generare 构成 regenerare「再次产生」，既用于生物，也用于精神更新。

items.en: Regeneration became a technical term in early Christian Latin for the new life of baptism, and this sense came into English first.
items.cn: regeneration 在早期基督教拉丁语中成为洗礼新生的术语，这一含义最先进入英语。

items.en: English adopted regeneration in the fourteenth century with the theological sense; the biological sense is recorded later.
items.cn: 英语于 14 世纪吸收 regeneration，先取神学义；生物学的含义记录得更晚。

items.en: Experimental work on hydra and planarians in the eighteenth century, and later cell biology, fixed the modern tissue sense.
items.cn: 18 世纪对水螅与涡虫的实验，以及后来的细胞生物学，确定了现代的组织再生义。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the same generare family; group two holds near meanings that differ in what is renewed.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 generare 词族的形近词；第二组是近义词，区别在于「更新的是什么」。

entries.definition: To grow again or renew. Regeneration is the process or result of that verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指重新长出或更新；regeneration 是该动词的过程或结果。

entries.definition: A single stage in a family line or a single act of producing. Without re- it lacks the idea of return.
entries.definitionCN: 指家族中的一代或一次产生行为；没有 re- 就不含「返回」之意。

entries.definition: Decline from a better to a worse state, built with de- 'down'. It is the mirror image of regeneration.
entries.definitionCN: 指由较好状态向较差状态衰退，由 de-「向下」构成，是 regeneration 的反面。

entries.definition: Describing the capacity to regrow, as in regenerative medicine. It modifies a noun rather than naming the process.
entries.definitionCN: 形容具有再生能力，如再生医学；它修饰名词，而不直接命名过程。

entries.definition: Active work that returns a site to a chosen earlier condition; regeneration can be unassisted.
entries.definitionCN: 通过主动工作把地点恢复到选定的旧状态；再生可以是无人协助的。

entries.definition: Making something fresh or valid again, used for licences, vows and city districts alike; it is broader and less biological.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物重新新鲜或重新有效，可用于执照、誓言与城区；范围更广，生物学色彩更弱。

entries.definition: The new growth itself, especially of plants. It names the visible result rather than the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 指新长出的部分本身，尤指植物；命名可见结果，而非整个过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'again' + generare 'to beget': a second birth.
normal.cn: re-「再一次」+ generare「生育」：第二次出生。

normal.en: The family runs generate, generation, regenerate, regeneration, regenerative, degenerate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 generate、generation、regenerate、regeneration、regenerative、degenerate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: tissue regeneration, forest regeneration, urban regeneration, natural regeneration.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：组织再生、森林更新、城市更新、天然更新。

normal.en: Forestry pairs it with seed trees: the parents left standing supply the next stand.
normal.cn: 林学把它与母树配对：留下的母树供给下一代林分。

normal.en: Medicine pairs it with degeneration: one grows back, the other wears down.
normal.cn: 医学把它与退变对举：一个长回来，一个磨损坏。

abstract.en: Picture a cut worm growing a new tail segment by segment.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被切断的蚯蚓一节一节长出新尾。

abstract.en: Picture a burnt hillside greening from the bottom up.
abstract.cn: 想象烧过的山坡自下而上重新变绿。

abstract.en: Picture an old factory chimney reused as a climbing wall.
abstract.cn: 想象旧厂房的烟囱被改作攀岩墙继续使用。

examples.en: The regeneration of the forest was slowed by heavy deer browsing.
examples.cn: 鹿的过度啃食拖慢了这片森林的更新。

examples.en: Stem-cell research aims at repairing organs through regeneration.
examples.cn: 干细胞研究旨在通过再生修复器官。

examples.en: Urban regeneration often displaces the residents it claims to help.
examples.cn: 城市更新常常让声称要帮助的原住民迁走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞（re）再生（generation）」——再来一次出生 → 组织再生、植被更新

root: 拉丁 re-「再一次」+ generare「生育」，源自 genus「出生、族类」→ regenerare「再次产生」；英语先取神学义，后固定生物学与城市更新义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a part or a place that was lost or worn out produces a new version of itself, from tissue and trees to districts, systems, populations, materials and memories.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：失去或耗损的部位与地方重新长出自身的新版本，从组织、林木到城区、系统、种群、材料与记忆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut stump pushing out a fresh green shoot from its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：被截断的树桩从断口边缘抽出新绿。

branches.en: TISSUE: the body regrows the part it lost.
branches.cn: 组织：身体重新长出失去的部位。

branches.en: FOREST AND POPULATION: stands and breeding groups produce their next generation.
branches.cn: 森林与种群：林分与繁殖群体产生下一代。

branches.en: SPIRIT: the earliest sense, a life given again from outside.
branches.cn: 灵魂：最早的含义，由外部再次赐予的生命。

branches.en: PLACE AND SYSTEM: districts and capacities are rebuilt rather than replaced.
branches.cn: 城区与系统：被重建而非替换的是街区与能力。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND MEMORY: what was spent or faded is made usable or audible again.
branches.cn: 材料与记忆：耗尽的重新可用，淡去的重新可闻。

intro.en: The noun joins the Latin prefix re- to the verb generare and takes the noun ending -ion; the whole family turns on the stem gener-.
intro.cn: 这个名词把拉丁前缀 re- 接在动词 generare 上，并带名词词尾 -ion；整个词族都围绕词干 gener- 展开。

latinIntro.en: Latin genus and generare yield generate, generation, regenerate, regeneration, regenerative, degenerate and generic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 genus 与 generare 衍生 generate、generation、regenerate、regeneration、regenerative、degenerate 与 generic。

items.meaning: the process of being brought forth again
items.example: Coral regeneration can take decades.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚的再生可能需要数十年。

items.example: The shrub regenerates after fire.
items.exampleCN: 这种灌木在火后能再生。

items.example: Regenerative farming rebuilds soil carbon.

items.meaning: a producing; one stage of descent
items.example: Each generation of pines is cut at sixty years.
items.exampleCN: 每一代松树在六十年时被采伐。

items.meaning: to produce or bring into being
items.example: The marsh generates its own peat.
items.exampleCN: 这片沼泽自行生成泥炭。

items.example: The backup generator started at once.

items.meaning: to fall from a former kind
items.example: The tissue degenerates without blood supply.
Generic names group the species.

definition_zh: 旋风；尘卷风；一连串迅疾的事件；情绪翻涌
definition_en: a mass of air turning rapidly around a moving centre, often lifting dust or loose material
core_image: 干草场上，风把尘土和草屑拧成一根旋转的柱子，贴着地面横冲过去
scene: 麦场上，一阵风把干草和尘土卷成一根旋转的柱子，老人指着说 A whirlwind crossed the yard and carried the straw over the fence.
sceneCN: 这里 whirlwind 指「绕移动中心快速旋转的气团」（第 1 个义项：能把尘土和轻物卷起的旋风）；句意为一阵旋风穿过院子，把稻草卷过了篱笆。

pos.zh: 旋风；尘卷风；一连串迅疾之事
旋风式的；极快的（如旋风式旅行）

collocations.zh: 旋风式旅行；走马观花的一趟
自食其果；收获自己种下的恶果

derivatives.zh: 旋风式旅行；行程极紧的访问

senses.title: Air turning rapidly around a centre
senses.titleCN: 旋风：绕中心快速旋转的气团
senses.definition: a body of air turning rapidly around a centre that moves across the ground
senses.definitionCN: 绕一个中心快速旋转、并沿地面移动的气团
senses.example: A whirlwind scattered the dry leaves across the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵旋风把干叶子吹散到公路上。
senses.why: Whirl names the turning and wind names the air, so the compound says exactly what it is: air that spins.
senses.whyCN: whirl 说「转」，wind 说「空气」，复合词正好说出它是什么：会转的空气。

senses.title: Dust devil
senses.titleCN: 尘卷风：看得见的尘土柱
senses.definition: a small, short-lived vortex made visible by the dust and debris it lifts
senses.definitionCN: 因卷起尘土与碎屑而可见的小型短命涡旋
senses.example: Dust devils danced along the empty road at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午时分，尘卷风在空荡的公路上跳跃。
senses.why: Once the vortex lifts loose material, the dust draws its outline, and the word names that visible column.
senses.whyCN: 涡旋卷起松软物质后，尘土勾出它的轮廓，这个词就指那根可见的柱子。

senses.title: A violent tornado-scale vortex
senses.definition: in older and literary usage, a large destructive whirlwind capable of tearing roofs away
senses.definitionCN: 在较早与文学用法中，指能掀掉屋顶的大型破坏性旋风
senses.example: The whirlwind tore the roof off the barn and flung it into the creek.
senses.exampleCN: 旋风掀掉谷仓的屋顶，把它甩进小河。
senses.why: Before tornado became the technical term, whirlwind covered the violent end of the scale, and the older sense survives in literature.
senses.whyCN: 在 tornado 成为术语之前，whirlwind 涵盖这一暴力极端，旧义仍留在文学中。

senses.title: Rapid succession of events
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：一连串迅疾的事件
senses.definition: a rapid, dizzying succession of events that leaves little time to rest
senses.definitionCN: 一连串迅速而令人眩晕、几乎没有喘息时间的事件
senses.example: The wedding was a whirlwind of meetings, forms and last-minute repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼成了一连串会面、表格与临时修补。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the spin: events arrive faster than they can be sorted, the way dust is swept up.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了旋转：事件来得比理清更快，就像尘土被卷起。

senses.title: Emotional turmoil
senses.definition: a confused, intense swirl of feelings that carries a person along
senses.definitionCN: 把人带着走的一团混乱而强烈的情绪
senses.example: She left the interview in a whirlwind of relief and doubt.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着宽慰与怀疑交织的翻涌情绪离开了面试。
senses.why: Feelings are described as air in motion: they circle, collide and refuse to settle.
senses.whyCN: 情绪被说成流动的空气：打转、相撞、不肯平息。

senses.title: Very fast, as an attributive
senses.titleCN: 定语用法：极快的、旋风式的
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean very fast and tightly packed, as in a whirlwind tour
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，表示极快且安排密集，如旋风式旅行
senses.example: They did a whirlwind tour of three capitals in five days.
senses.exampleCN: 他们五天内旋风式地游了三座首都。
senses.why: The speed of the vortex becomes the defining quality of the trip, so the noun turns into a modifier.
senses.whyCN: 涡旋的速度成了这趟旅行的定义特征，于是名词变成修饰语。

senses.title: Biblical and literary tempest
senses.definition: a destructive tempest used as an image of judgment, as in the phrase reap the whirlwind
senses.definitionCN: 作为审判意象的破坏性暴风，如短语「自食其果」所示
senses.example: The prophet warned that the nation would reap the whirlwind.
senses.exampleCN: 先知警告说，这个民族将自食其果。
senses.why: Scriptural language uses the storm as a picture of consequences arriving with irresistible force.
senses.whyCN: 圣经语言用风暴比喻以不可阻挡之势到来的后果。

senses.title: A swirling mass of loose material
senses.definition: the swirling load itself, such as leaves, dust or flame carried up in a circle
senses.definitionCN: 被卷起旋转的物质本身，如树叶、尘土或火焰
senses.example: A whirlwind of leaves followed the children down the lane.
senses.exampleCN: 一团旋转的树叶跟着孩子们跑下小径。
senses.why: The container and the contents trade places: the wind is named by the visible mass it carries.
senses.whyCN: 容器与内容互换：风用它携带的可见物质来命名。

intro.en: Whirlwind is a native English compound of whirl and wind. Whirl came from Old Norse, wind from Old English; the compound is recorded from the fourteenth century, and the figurative use is later.
intro.cn: whirlwind 是英语本土复合词，由 whirl 与 wind 合成。whirl 来自古诺斯语，wind 来自古英语；复合词约 14 世纪见于记载，比喻用法更晚。

items.en: Old Norse hvirfla meant 'to turn round, whirl', and the noun hvirfill named a ring, a circle or a whirlpool.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 hvirfla 意为「旋转、打转」，名词 hvirfill 指环、圆圈或漩涡。

items.en: The ancestor is reconstructed as *hwerb- or *hwerfl- 'to turn'; German wirbeln 'to whirl' and Dutch wervelen descend from the same reconstructed form.
items.cn: 更早的祖形被重构为 *hwerb- 或 *hwerfl-，意为「转」；德语 wirbeln「旋转」与荷兰语 wervelen 都出自同一重构形式。

items.en: Old English wind 'wind' goes back to Proto-Germanic *windaz, generally connected with a root meaning 'to blow'.
items.cn: 古英语 wind「风」上溯到原始日耳曼语 *windaz，一般与表示「吹」的词根相联系。

items.en: The compound whirlwind is recorded in Middle English; the exact first occurrence is uncertain, and the word competed with other native terms for the same weather.
items.cn: 复合词 whirlwind 见于中古英语；确切的最早书证不确定，这个词曾与其他本土说法竞争同一天气现象。

items.en: The figurative senses, a whirlwind of events and a whirlwind tour, belong to later literary and journalistic usage.
items.cn: 比喻义——一连串事件与旋风式旅行——属于较晚的文学与新闻用法。

note.en: The first group is built from the same or similar pieces but means something else; the second group holds the rotating-weather family.
note.cn: 第一组由相同或相近的成分构成，但意思不同；第二组是旋转天气家族。

entries.definition: A building with sails turned by the wind to grind grain or pump water; the second element is a machine, not spinning air.
entries.definitionCN: 用风转动叶片来磨粮或抽水的建筑；第二成分是机器，不是旋转的空气。

entries.definition: From Old Norse vindauga 'wind eye', an opening for air and light; it shares wind but not the whirling.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古诺斯语 vindauga「风眼」，通风透光的开口；同有 wind，但没有旋转义。

entries.definition: A spinning body of water; the same whirl element with pool instead of wind.
entries.definitionCN: 旋转的水体；同一 whirl 成分，但换成 pool 而非 wind。

entries.definition: The present participle of the verb whirl 'to turn quickly'; it describes the action, not the weather system.
entries.definitionCN: 动词 whirl「快速旋转」的现在分词；描述动作，不是天气系统。

entries.definition: The technical term for a violent vortex touching the ground from a thundercloud; narrower and more formal than whirlwind.
entries.definitionCN: 从雷暴云触地的猛烈涡旋的技术术语；比 whirlwind 更窄、更正式。

entries.definition: A large low-pressure system whose winds rotate around a centre; far larger than a whirlwind.
entries.definitionCN: 风绕中心旋转的大型低压系统；比旋风大得多。

entries.definition: The usual name for a small, fair-weather whirlwind made visible by dust.
entries.definitionCN: 晴好天气下由尘土显形的小型旋风的常用名称。

entries.definition: A sudden brief increase in wind; it pushes in a straight line rather than turning in a circle.
entries.definitionCN: 风的突然短暂加强；是直线推进而非绕圈旋转。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real halves of the compound, real fixed phrases and the real rotating-weather family, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词两个真实成分、真实固定搭配与真实旋转天气词族，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: whirl 'turn quickly' + wind 'moving air': the word is its own definition.
normal.cn: whirl「快转」+ wind「流动的空气」：这个词就是自己的定义。

normal.en: The same whirl sits in whirlpool and whirligig.
normal.cn: 同一个 whirl 在 whirlpool 与 whirligig 里。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: whirlwind tour, whirlwind romance, whirlwind of change.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：旋风式旅行、闪电式恋情、急剧变化。

normal.en: Reap the whirlwind means suffer the consequences of what you did.
normal.cn: reap the whirlwind 意为自食其果。

normal.en: As an adjective it always means very fast, never calm.
normal.cn: 作形容词时永远表示极快，从不表示平静。

abstract.en: Picture a straw hat lifted and hung in the air for a moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶草帽被卷起，在空中悬停片刻。

abstract.en: Picture a week so full that it feels like one long spin.
abstract.cn: 想象一周忙得像一场漫长的旋转。

abstract.en: Picture feelings circling so fast that none of them can land.
abstract.cn: 想象情绪转得太快，哪一种都落不下来。

examples.en: A whirlwind lifted the tarpaulin and dropped it on the shed roof.
examples.cn: 一阵旋风把防水布卷起，又把它扔到棚顶上。

examples.en: The delegation returned from a whirlwind tour of four cities.
examples.cn: 代表团结束了对四座城市的旋风式访问后返回。

examples.en: Her first term was a whirlwind of lectures, labs and exams.
examples.cn: 她的第一个学期是一场讲座、实验与考试的旋风。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「涡轮」——涡旋像轮子一样转，转出一阵贴地的风

root: 英语本土复合词：whirl 来自古诺斯语 hvirfla「旋转」（更早祖形一般重构为 *hwerb-/*hwerfl-「转」），wind 来自古英语 wind，上溯原始日耳曼语 *windaz。构词与来源清楚；复合词最早书证约 14 世纪，具体年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the same turning: a spinning volume of air, its visible dust column, the violent large vortex, a rush of events, a swirl of feelings, the fast modifier, the biblical tempest and the swirling load itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个旋转展开：旋转的气团、可见的尘土柱、猛烈的大涡旋、事件的一阵急转、情绪的翻涌、表示极快的定语、圣经式暴风，以及被卷起旋转的物质本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dust and straw twisted into a spinning column that travels across a field.
core.cn: 核心意象：尘土与稻草被拧成一根旋转的柱子，横穿田野移动。

branches.en: WIND AND LOAD: the spinning air and the material it carries take turns being the referent.
branches.cn: 风与被卷物：旋转的空气与它携带的材料轮流充当所指对象。

branches.en: SMALL AND LARGE: a dust devil and a roof-tearing vortex are the two ends of one scale.
branches.cn: 小与大：尘卷风与掀屋顶的涡旋是同一尺度的两端。

branches.en: FAST TIME: a rush of events and a whirlwind tour both make time feel spun.
branches.cn: 飞快的时间：事件急转与旋风式旅行都让时间像被旋转起来。

branches.en: INNER WEATHER: emotions circle and collide like air in a vortex.
branches.cn: 内心天气：情绪像涡旋里的空气一样打转、相撞。

branches.en: JUDGMENT: scripture turns the storm into an image of consequences.
branches.cn: 审判：圣经把风暴变成后果的意象。

intro.en: Whirlwind is a compound, not a suffixed word: whirl plus wind. Its productive life is in phrases such as whirlwind tour and whirlwind romance.
intro.cn: whirlwind 是复合词而非加后缀的词：whirl 加 wind。它的构词活力在 whirlwind tour、whirlwind romance 这类短语里。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin cognate here. Whirl is Germanic and wind is Germanic; Latin expresses the same idea with turbo and vortex, which are semantic counterparts rather than relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁同族词。whirl 属日耳曼语，wind 也属日耳曼语；拉丁语用 turbo 与 vortex 表达同一概念，那是语义对应词而非同族词。

items.meaning: a spinning toy or a merry-go-round
items.example: The child spun the whirligig on the path.
items.exampleCN: 孩子在路上转动旋转玩具。

items.example: The band played a whirlwind tour of six countries.

items.meaning: a relationship that starts and intensifies very quickly
items.meaningCN: 开始与升温都极快的恋情
items.example: Their whirlwind romance ended in a summer wedding.
items.exampleCN: 他们的闪电式恋情以一场夏季婚礼结束。

items.structure: the second element of the compound, identical to the noun wind
items.example: The second half keeps its literal meaning.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分保留了字面义。

definition_zh: 厌倦享乐的；见惯不惊的；麻木不以为意的
definition_en: unimpressed or bored because you have experienced too much of something
core_image: 坐在VIP席上看烟花却不抬头的人
scene: 老记者看惯了大场面，烟花在他头顶炸开也没抬眼。 The jaded critics were blase about the new film.
sceneCN: 这里 blase 是「见惯不惊的」（第 1 个义项：因阅历过多而不再兴奋）；句意是这些看腻了的影评人对新片提不起兴趣。

pos.zh: 厌倦的；麻木的；不以为意的

collocations.zh: 见多识广而不再惊讶的城里人

derivatives.zh: blase 加 -ness，义为「厌倦麻木的状态」
口语化副词，义为「无动于衷地」

senses.title: Bored from overexposure
senses.definition: unexcited because one has seen or done something too many times
senses.definitionCN: 因见得太多、做得太多而不再兴奋
senses.example: The jaded critics were blase about the new film.
senses.exampleCN: 这些看腻了的影评人对新片提不起兴趣。
senses.why: French blaser meant to sate or wear out by indulgence, and the word keeps that spent feeling.
senses.whyCN: 法语 blaser 本指纵欲过度而疲乏，该词保留了那种「耗尽」的感觉。

senses.title: Unimpressed by luxury
senses.definition: no longer excited by wealth, comfort, or glamour
senses.definitionCN: 对财富、舒适或光环不再心动
senses.example: Born to palaces, the prince was blase about gold.
senses.exampleCN: 生于宫殿的王子对黄金早已无感。
senses.why: What surrounds you daily stops dazzling, as candlelight fades at noon.
senses.whyCN: 日日环绕之物不再炫目，如烛火在正午失色。

senses.title: Affecting cool indifference
senses.definition: acting worldly and unexcitable, sometimes as a pose
senses.definitionCN: 表现得老练淡漠，有时是装出来的姿态
senses.example: He tried to seem blase, but his hands shook.
senses.exampleCN: 他努力装出满不在乎的样子，手却在发抖。
senses.why: The spent look became a style, worn even by those still fresh.
senses.whyCN: 「阅尽千帆」的模样成了一种做派，连初出茅庐者也披上它。

senses.title: Cynically unresponsive to appeals
senses.definition: unmoved by warnings, appeals, or shock
senses.definitionCN: 对警告、呼吁或惊人之事无动于衷
senses.example: Voters have grown blase about scandal headlines.
senses.exampleCN: 选民对丑闻标题已经麻木。
senses.why: Repeated shock loses its sting, and the mind stops answering.
senses.whyCN: 反复的惊吓失去刺感，心便不再应答。

senses.title: Weary of pleasure itself
senses.definition: tired of amusements once loved
senses.definitionCN: 对曾经热爱的娱乐感到疲倦
senses.example: Parties that once thrilled her now left her blase.
senses.exampleCN: 曾令她兴奋的派对如今只让她倦怠。
senses.why: Indulgence wears out appetite; the feast ends in yawns.
senses.whyCN: 纵情耗尽胃口，盛宴终以呵欠收场。

senses.title: Casually dismissive of danger
senses.definition: treating risk with bored unconcern
senses.definitionCN: 以倦怠的漠然对待风险
senses.example: The pilot was blase about the storm warning.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员对风暴警报满不在乎。
senses.why: A veteran of danger stops counting it, and carelessness follows.
senses.whyCN: 身经百险者不再点数危险，随之而来的是轻忽。

senses.title: Detached in social style
senses.definition: socially aloof and hard to impress
senses.definitionCN: 社交场合疏离、难以取悦
senses.example: The blase regulars barely glanced at the newcomers.
senses.exampleCN: 那些淡漠的老客对新人几乎不屑一顾。
senses.why: Indifference is a wall the satiated build around themselves.
senses.whyCN: 冷漠是餍足者为自己筑起的墙。

senses.title: Emotionally flat from modern media
senses.definition: numbed by the constant stream of images and news
senses.definitionCN: 被持续不断的图像与新闻磨钝了感受力
senses.example: Constant feeds make audiences blase even about disaster.
senses.exampleCN: 不间断的信息流让观众连灾难都麻木了。
senses.why: The modern flood of spectacle repeats the old overindulgence at scale.
senses.whyCN: 现代景象的洪流把旧日的纵欲放大重演。

intro.en: Blase is French blaser, to sate or wear out by indulgence.
intro.cn: blase 来自法语 blaser「因纵情享乐而餍足疲乏」。

items.en: blaser is first recorded in the 17th century; its deeper origin is uncertain, possibly from Middle Dutch or a literary coinage.
items.cn: blaser 首见于 17 世纪法语，更早来源不确定，或出自中古荷兰语，或系文人造词。

items.en: the word spread through 19th-century French literature describing world-weary characters.
items.cn: 该词经 19 世纪法国文学中厌世人物的描写而流行。

items.en: English borrowed blase in the 19th century for world-weary sophistication.
items.cn: 英语于 19 世纪借入 blase，指看破世情的老练倦怠。

items.en: the sense widened to any bored unresponsiveness.
items.cn: 20 世纪词义扩大，泛指各类麻木不以为意。

items.en: now common in media criticism of numb audiences.
items.cn: 今常用于批评被信息洪流磨钝的受众。

note.en: Blase has no English relatives; the look-alike group collects similar-sounding words, and the near-meaning group gathers weary-indifference words.
note.cn: blase 在英语中无同族词；形近组收音近词，近义组收倦怠淡漠类词。

definition_zh: 露头；岩层露出地表的部分；露出地表
definition_en: the part of a rock layer that can be seen at the surface, or to appear at the surface in this way
core_image: 草坡被雨水冲开一块，灰白色岩层断面从土里露出一角
scene: 山坡上的草被雨水冲开一块，露出灰白色的岩层断面： A small outcrop of limestone appeared where the soil had washed away.
sceneCN: 这里 outcrop 指「岩层在地表露出的部分」（第 1 个义项：基岩或岩层在地表可见的一块）；句意为土壤被冲走的地方露出一小片石灰岩露头。

pos.zh: 露头；岩层出露部分（可数，复数为 outcrops）
出露；露出地表（outcrops, outcropped, outcropping）

senses.title: Rock visible at the surface
senses.titleCN: 岩层在地表露出的部分
senses.definition: a place where rock that is normally buried can be seen at the earth's surface
senses.definitionCN: 原本埋在地下的岩石在地表可见的地方
senses.example: A small outcrop of limestone appeared where the soil had washed away.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤被冲走的地方露出一小片石灰岩露头。
senses.why: Out plus crop pictures something breaking through the surface, like a plant top pushing out of the ground.
senses.whyCN: out 加 crop 描绘某物破土而出，像植物的顶端从地面钻出。

senses.title: To appear at the surface
senses.definition: of rock, to reach the surface and become visible there
senses.definitionCN: 指岩层到达地表并在那里可见
senses.example: The granite outcrops along the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 花岗岩沿山脊出露。
senses.why: The verb keeps the same image but focuses on the event of breaking through rather than the patch left behind.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留同一意象，但聚焦于破土这一事件，而非留下的那片露头。

senses.title: A patch seen in a field
senses.titleCN: 野外可见的一小片露头
senses.definition: a limited patch of bedrock visible between soil, grass, or snow
senses.definitionCN: 土壤、草或雪之间可见的一小片基岩
senses.example: The shepherd knew every outcrop on the hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 牧羊人熟悉山坡上每一处露头。
senses.why: In fieldwork an outcrop is what you can actually put your hand on; everything else is inference.
senses.whyCN: 在野外工作中，露头是你真正能摸到的部分，其余都靠推断。

senses.title: An isolated exposure of one layer
senses.definition: a small isolated place where one particular stratum can be examined
senses.definitionCN: 可对某一特定层位进行观察的一小块孤立出露处
senses.example: The sandstone outcrop is the only place where the lower layer can be studied.
senses.exampleCN: 这处砂岩露头是研究下层的唯一地点。
senses.why: A single window into a buried layer is enough to measure its thickness and dip.
senses.whyCN: 观察埋藏层位的一扇小窗，就足以测量其厚度与倾角。

senses.title: The edge of a coal or ore seam
senses.definition: the surface end of a mineral seam where it meets the ground
senses.definitionCN: 矿层与地面相接的地表端
senses.example: Miners followed the coal outcrop into the hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工沿着煤层露头掘进山体。
senses.why: Prospectors begin where a seam shows itself, because the visible end points toward the buried body.
senses.whyCN: 勘探者从矿层自己显露的一端开始，因为可见的端头指向埋藏的主体。

senses.title: A projecting rock on a slope
senses.definition: a rock mass that sticks out from a slope or cliff face
senses.definitionCN: 从坡面或崖面突出来的岩体
senses.example: A grey outcrop barred the path along the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 一处灰色露头挡住崖边小路。
senses.why: The word also describes the shape that stands out, not only the fact that it is visible.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也描述突出来的形状，而不只是「可见」这一事实。

senses.title: A coral or reef exposure
senses.definition: a mass of reef rock that rises above the surrounding sediment or water
senses.definitionCN: 高出周围沉积物或水面的礁岩体
senses.example: A coral outcrop broke the surface at low tide.
senses.exampleCN: 退潮时一处珊瑚礁体露出水面。
senses.why: The same geometry applies underwater: whatever rises above its surroundings becomes visible.
senses.whyCN: 同一几何关系适用于水下：高出周围的部分就会显露出来。

senses.title: Figurative: something surfacing
senses.definition: a visible sign of something that was previously hidden or unspoken
senses.definitionCN: 先前隐藏或未被言明之物显露出来的可见迹象
senses.example: The protest was an outcrop of years of quiet resentment.
senses.exampleCN: 这场抗议是多年沉默怨气的一次显露。
senses.why: The metaphor treats feelings as strata: most stay buried, and what shows at the surface is only a patch.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把情绪当作地层：大部分仍埋着，露出地表的只是一小块。

senses.title: A visible portion of a larger whole
senses.titleCN: 整体中可见的一小部分
senses.definition: the small part of a larger body that can be observed directly
senses.definitionCN: 较大整体中可直接观察到的一小部分
senses.example: The visible outcrop is a tiny sample of the granite below.
senses.exampleCN: 可见的露头只是下方花岗岩的一小份样本。
senses.why: Field geology reasons from windows: the outcrop is evidence, and the formation is the hidden whole.
senses.whyCN: 野外地质学从窗口推理：露头是证据，地层是隐藏的整体。

intro.en: Outcrop is an English compound of out and crop, coined for geology in the nineteenth century. Its parts are clear, but the exact first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: outcrop 是 out 与 crop 的英语复合词，19 世纪为地质学而造。各部分清楚，但确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Crop meant the top of a plant or an ear of grain, from Proto-Germanic kruppaz. The idea is a rounded head standing above the ground.
items.cn: crop 原指植物顶端或谷穗，来自原始日耳曼语 kruppaz。其意象是高出地面的圆头。

items.en: To crop out meant to show itself at the surface, as a stratum does where soil has worn away.
items.cn: crop out 原指在地表显露出来，正如土壤被蚀去处的地层。

items.en: Geologists turned the verb phrase into the noun outcrop in the nineteenth century; the earliest citation is not fixed, so the date is uncertain.
items.cn: 地质学家在 19 世纪把动词短语转为名词 outcrop；最早书证未固定，因此年代存疑。

items.en: Because buried rock can only be sampled where it crops out, the word became basic vocabulary of field mapping.
items.cn: 由于埋藏岩石只能在出露处采样，这个词成了野外填图的基本词汇。

items.en: The figurative sense of anything surfacing is modern and informal; no single first use is recorded.
items.cn: 任何事物显露的比喻义属现代口语用法，没有单一的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds field and mapping words that are routinely interchanged with outcrop; group two holds words for exposed rock or bare ground.
note.cn: 第一组是常与 outcrop 互换的野外与填图用词；第二组是裸露岩石或裸地的词。

entries.definition: A variant noun or adjective meaning the same exposure; it often describes a mass that projects from a slope.
entries.definitionCN: 同义的变体名词或形容词，指同一出露；常描述从坡面突出的岩体。

entries.definition: The verb phrase behind the noun: a layer crops out where it reaches the surface.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词短语：岩层到达地表处就出露。

entries.definition: Any place where a rock body is open to view, including quarries and road cuts; outcrop is the natural surface case.
entries.definitionCN: 岩体可供观察的任何地点，包括采石场与路堑；outcrop 特指自然地表的情形。

entries.definition: Not an English word. The vowel in the second syllable is o, not e, so outcrop should not be written outerop.
entries.definitionCN: 并非英语词。第二音节的元音是 o 而非 e，因此不能写成 outerop。

entries.definition: The solid rock beneath soil; it may be exposed as an outcrop or remain covered.
entries.definitionCN: 土壤之下的坚固岩石；它可作为露头露出，也可仍被覆盖。

entries.definition: A detached block of rock; unlike an outcrop, it is not attached to the parent body.
entries.definitionCN: 脱离母岩的石块；与露头不同，它不与母体相连。

entries.definition: A steep face of rock; an outcrop may form part of a cliff but need not be vertical.
entries.definitionCN: 陡峭岩面；露头可以是崖壁的一部分，但不必垂直。

entries.definition: Ground with no vegetation or soil cover; it may be soil or gravel, not necessarily rock.
entries.definitionCN: 没有植被或土壤覆盖的地面，可能是土或砾石，不一定是岩石。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real English morphemes, real field terms and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实英语语素、真实野外术语与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Out + crop: the rock crops out of the ground like a plant top.
normal.cn: out 加 crop：岩石像植物顶端一样从地里长出来。

normal.en: A formation is the whole body; an outcrop is only the window onto it.
normal.cn: formation 是整体岩体，outcrop 只是观察它的窗口。

normal.en: Field geologists say the layer crops out in the stream bed.
normal.cn: 野外地质学家说岩层在河床出露。

normal.en: Outcrops are mapped as lines or patches, because they are edges of buried bodies.
normal.cn: 露头在地图上被画成线或斑块，因为它们是埋藏岩体的边缘。

normal.en: Coal seams are traced from their outcrop inward.
normal.cn: 煤层从露头向内部追索。

abstract.en: Picture a buried pipe with one joint poking through the paving.
abstract.cn: 想象一根埋在地下的管道，只有一个接头从路面探出。

abstract.en: Picture an iceberg showing only its tip above the water.
abstract.cn: 想象一座冰山只把尖端露在水面。

abstract.en: Picture an old argument surfacing years later in a single sharp remark.
abstract.cn: 想象多年前的争执，多年后因一句尖刻的话而浮出水面。

examples.en: A small outcrop of limestone appeared where the soil had washed away.
examples.cn: 土壤被冲走的地方露出一小片石灰岩露头。

examples.en: The geologist measured the dip at the only outcrop in the valley.
examples.cn: 地质学家在山谷中唯一的露头处测量了倾角。

examples.en: Granite outcrops all along the ridge, so the bedrock is easy to sample.
examples.cn: 花岗岩沿山脊到处出露，因此基岩易于采样。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特克罗普」——一块从土里探出头的岩石 → 露头、出露

root: 英语 out「向外」+ crop「植物顶端、谷穗」（原始日耳曼语 kruppaz）；19 世纪地质学用作「岩层出露」，属英语本族复合词，无拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses start from a patch of surfaced rock and extend to seams, reefs, slopes, and finally to anything hidden that becomes briefly visible.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一片露出地表的岩石出发，延伸到矿层、礁体、坡面，最后落到一切短暂显露的隐藏之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey rock face breaking through grass where the soil has worn away.
core.cn: 核心意象：土壤被蚀去处，灰白岩面从草地里破出。

branches.en: PATCH AND WINDOW: the visible patch is also the only place where the buried body can be examined.
branches.cn: 露出的一片与窗口：可见的一片，也是检查埋藏岩体的唯一地点。

branches.en: EVENT: the verb turns the patch into an act of reaching the surface.
branches.cn: 事件：动词把这片露头转为到达地表的行为。

branches.en: SAMPLE OF A WHOLE: one exposure stands for a body far larger than what is seen.
branches.cn: 整体的样本：一处露头代表远比所见更大的岩体。

branches.en: EDGE AND RISE: seams and reefs both show where a mass meets the surface.
branches.cn: 边缘与隆起：矿层与礁体都显示岩体与地表相接之处。

branches.en: PROJECTION AND METAPHOR: what sticks out is what gets noticed, in rock and in feeling alike.
branches.cn: 突出与比喻：无论是岩石还是情绪，突出来的部分才被注意到。

intro.en: Outcrop is a transparent English compound, so its two halves can be read directly.
intro.cn: outcrop 是透明的英语复合词，两半可直接读出。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English in both parts, so no Latin source form stands behind it; the table below therefore records no Latin relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的两部分都是英语本族语，背后没有拉丁语源形式，因此下表不列拉丁同族词。

items.example: Out- marks something moving into view.
items.exampleCN: out- 标记某物进入视野。

items.structure: Old English crop (top of a plant, ear of grain)
items.meaning: the visible top of a growing thing
items.example: The wheat crop stood above the soil.
The outcrop is the only exposure for miles.
items.exampleCN: 这处露头是数英里内唯一的出露。

items.example: An outcropping of schist blocked the trail.
items.exampleCN: 一片片岩露头挡住了小径。

items.example: The seam crops out beside the road.
The cropland lies on deep soil, not on rock.
items.exampleCN: 耕地位于深厚土壤上，而非岩石上。

items.meaning: a placing out; a place open to view
items.example: The road cut provides a fresh exposure.
items.exampleCN: 路堑提供了一处新鲜剖面。

items.example: Bedrock shows through the thin soil.

definition_en: the number of people or organisms in a given area, usually per square kilometre
core_image: 同样大的两格方框，一格挤满小点，另一格只有零星几点
scene: 这里指「人口密度」。 The district's population density doubled within a decade.
sceneCN: 这里 population density 指「单位面积上的人口数」（第 1 个义项：每平方公里等面积内居住的人数）；句意为该区的人口密度在十年内翻倍。图中可辨识物件：等大的两格方框、密集的小点与稀疏的小点、比例尺、名册计数。

pos.zh: 人口密度；种群密度（不可数，指具体数值时可有复数 densities）

forms.label: 复数（不同地区或不同数值）

senses.title: People per unit of land
senses.definition: the number of people living in each unit of land area
senses.definitionCN: 每一单位土地面积上居住的人数
senses.example: The district's population density doubled within a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 该区的人口密度在十年内翻倍。
senses.why: population supplies the count and density supplies the division by area, so the phrase is simply people divided by space.
senses.whyCN: population 提供人数，density 提供按面积相除，因此这个短语就是人数除以空间。

senses.title: The arithmetic measure
senses.titleCN: 算术密度：总人口除以总面积
senses.definition: total population divided by total land area, the simplest of the measures
senses.definitionCN: 总人口除以总土地面积，是最简单的度量
senses.example: Arithmetic population density hides the fact that most of the land is desert.
senses.exampleCN: 算术人口密度掩盖了大部分土地是沙漠这一事实。
senses.why: the plain quotient is easy to compute and easy to mislead, which is why geographers keep naming it separately.
senses.whyCN: 这个朴素商数易算也易误导，因此地理学者要单独给它一个名称。

senses.title: People per farmable land
senses.titleCN: 生理密度：人口除以可耕地
senses.definition: population divided by the area of arable land, showing pressure on farmland
senses.definitionCN: 人口除以可耕地面积，显示对农田的压力
senses.example: Physiological population density is far higher than the arithmetic figure.
senses.exampleCN: 生理人口密度远高于算术数字。
senses.why: swapping total land for arable land shows how many mouths depend on each field, which is the point of the second measure.
senses.whyCN: 把总面积换成可耕地，就能看出每块田养多少张嘴，这正是第二种度量的用意。

senses.title: Farmers per farmland
senses.titleCN: 农业密度：农业人口除以农地
senses.definition: the number of farmers per unit of farmland, an indicator of labour intensity
senses.definitionCN: 每单位农地上的农民数，用以显示劳动集约程度
senses.example: Agricultural population density fell as machines replaced hands.
senses.exampleCN: 机器取代人力后，农业人口密度下降。
senses.why: counting farmers rather than eaters measures labour intensity, so the same word serves a different question.
senses.whyCN: 数农民而不是数吃饭的人，衡量的是劳动强度，因此同一个词服务另一个问题。

senses.title: Organisms per habitat area
senses.titleCN: 生态密度：单位生境面积的个体数
senses.definition: the number of organisms of a species in each unit of habitat
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种在每单位生境中的个体数
senses.example: Population density of the frogs peaked in the reed bed.
senses.exampleCN: 这些蛙的种群密度在芦苇丛中达到峰值。
senses.why: ecologists divide by usable habitat rather than by map area, which is why the animal version often differs sharply from the human one.
senses.whyCN: 生态学者除以可用生境而非地图面积，因此动物版本常与人版本差别很大。

senses.title: Crowding in built-up areas
senses.definition: the intensity of people per built area, used in planning and housing
senses.definitionCN: 每单位建成区的人口强度，用于规划与住房
senses.example: The city raised building heights to cut population density at ground level.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市提高建筑高度，以降低地面层的人口密度。
senses.why: planning divides by the built area rather than the whole municipal area, and vertical growth changes the quotient.
senses.whyCN: 规划除以建成区而非整个市域，而向上生长会改变这个商数。

senses.title: Density-dependent effects
senses.definition: the way crowding changes birth rates, death rates or disease spread
senses.definitionCN: 拥挤程度如何改变出生率、死亡率或疾病传播
senses.example: Disease spreads faster where population density is high.
senses.exampleCN: 人口密度高的地方疾病传播更快。
senses.why: when the number itself changes survival, biologists call the effect density-dependent, turning the measure into a cause.
senses.whyCN: 当这个数字本身改变了存活，生物学家称之为密度制约，把度量变成了原因。

senses.title: A planning metric
senses.titleCN: 规划指标：用于分区与配建
senses.definition: a figure used to set zoning, transport and service provision
senses.definitionCN: 用于确定分区、交通与公共服务的指标
senses.example: The zoning code ties bus frequency to population density.
senses.exampleCN: 分区规范把公交频次与人口密度挂钩。
senses.why: a number that can be mapped and compared becomes a rule of thumb for services, which is how it ends up in codes.
senses.whyCN: 一个可制图、可比较的数字会成为配建经验法则，于是进入规范条文。

intro.en: Population is Latin populus 'people' through populatio; density comes from Latin densitas, from densus 'thick, crowded'. The phrase is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: population 经 populatio 来自拉丁 populus「人民」；density 来自拉丁 densitas，源自 densus「稠密、拥挤」。这个短语是近代组合。年代均为约数。

items.en: Densus meant 'thick, crowded, close-set'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link sometimes drawn to a root meaning 'dense' is a reconstruction.
items.cn: densus 意为「稠密、拥挤、排得紧」。其更深来源不确定；把它连到某个表示「稠密」的词根只是重构。

items.en: Densitas named thickness or closeness; English density entered in the sixteenth century through science.
items.cn: densitas 指浓厚或紧密；英语 density 于 16 世纪经科学语境进入。

items.en: Populus 'people' gave populatio 'a peopling, a multitude', and English population.
items.cn: populus「人民」给出 populatio「人群、使有人居住」与英语 population。

items.en: The compound population density spread in the nineteenth century, when censuses were mapped onto land area.
items.cn: 组合 population density 在 19 世纪扩散，当时人口普查结果被叠到土地面积上。

items.en: The twentieth century extended the figure from people to animals and plants, giving the ecological sense.
items.cn: 20 世纪把这个数值从人扩展到动植物，形成生态义。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest use of the exact compound is not precisely recorded, and the origins of densus and populus both remain unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这一确切组合的最早使用没有精确记录；densus 与 populus 的来源都仍无定论。

note.en: Group one holds measures of density that are constantly confused in geography; group two holds related spatial ideas.
note.cn: 第一组是地理学中常被混淆的几种密度度量；第二组是相关的空间概念。

entries.definition: Total population divided by total area; it ignores which land can actually be used.
entries.definitionCN: 总人口除以总面积；不考虑土地是否可用。

entries.definition: Population divided by arable land; it measures pressure on the land that feeds people.
entries.definitionCN: 人口除以可耕地；衡量养活人口的土地承受的压力。

entries.definition: Farmers divided by farmland; it indicates how labour-intensive farming is.
entries.definitionCN: 农民数除以农地；显示农业的劳动集约程度。

entries.definition: Organisms divided by the area they can actually inhabit; it is the biological form of the measure.
entries.definitionCN: 生物数除以它们实际可栖居的面积；是这一度量的生物学形态。

entries.definition: The experience of too many people in too little space; density is the number, crowding is its effect.
entries.definitionCN: 指空间过小而人过多的体验；density 是数字，crowding 是其效果。

entries.definition: The gathering of things into one area; it names the pattern, not the rate per unit.
entries.definitionCN: 指事物聚到一处；命名格局，而非单位面积比率。

entries.definition: How a population is spread across space; density is one number from that spread.
entries.definitionCN: 指人口在空间上如何散布；density 是这一散布得出的一个数。

entries.definition: The maximum number an area can support; density is where the population actually sits.
entries.definitionCN: 指某地可支撑的最大数量；density 是种群实际所处的位置。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: population 'count' + density 'thickness': how thick people lie on the land.
normal.cn: population「计数」+ density「浓稠度」：人在地上铺得多厚。

normal.en: The family runs dense, densely, density, densify, population.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 dense、densely、density、densify、population。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the measures: arithmetic density, physiological density, agricultural density.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各种度量：算术密度、生理密度、农业密度。

normal.en: The unit is always people per area, so the phrase is a division problem.
normal.cn: 单位始终是每面积多少人，因此这个短语就是一道除法。

normal.en: Ecologists say density-dependent when crowding itself changes survival.
normal.cn: 生态学用 density-dependent 指拥挤本身改变了存活。

abstract.en: Picture two equal boxes, one packed with dots and one nearly empty.
abstract.cn: 想象两个同样大的方框，一个挤满小点，一个几乎空白。

abstract.en: Picture a lift that holds twelve and thirty people get in.
abstract.cn: 想象一部限载十二人的电梯挤进三十人。

abstract.en: Picture a map where colour deepens as the dots multiply.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，小点越多颜色越深。

examples.en: Population density is highest along the river mouths.
examples.cn: 人口密度在河口一带最高。

examples.en: The map shades population density in five bands.
examples.cn: 这幅图用五个色阶表示人口密度。

examples.en: High population density makes contact tracing harder.
examples.cn: 高人口密度让接触者追踪更困难。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「population（人口）+ density（密度）」——同样大的地方挤了多少人 → 人口密度

root: 拉丁 populus「人民」（来源不确定）+ populatio「人群」+ 拉丁 densitas「浓厚」来自 densus「稠密」（更深来源不确定）；英语 population density。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one division: a count is divided by an area, and the quotient is then read as arithmetic, physiological, agricultural, ecological, urban, epidemiological and finally as a planning number.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次除法展开：用面积去除人数，所得的商再被读成算术、生理、农业、生态、城市、流行病学，最后成为规划数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two equal boxes, one crowded with dots and one sparse.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个同样大的方框，一个挤满小点，一个稀疏。

branches.en: PLAIN DIVISION: total people over total land, the first measure taught.
branches.cn: 朴素除法：总人口除以总土地，最先教的那个度量。

branches.en: LAND THAT FEEDS: divide by arable land, and again by the farmers on it.
branches.cn: 养人的土地：先除以可耕地，再除以地上的农民。

branches.en: HABITAT VERSION: the same quotient applied to animals and plants.
branches.cn: 生境版本：同一商数用于动植物。

branches.en: BUILT SPACE AND PLANS: heights, zoning and bus routes respond to the number.
branches.cn: 建成空间与规划：层高、分区与公交线路都随这个数调整。

branches.en: DENSITY-DEPENDENT: crowding itself changes births, deaths and contagion.
branches.cn: 密度制约：拥挤本身改变出生、死亡与传染。

intro.en: The phrase joins two Latin-derived nouns; density carries the suffix -ity, which turns the adjective densus into a measurable noun.
intro.cn: 这个短语把两个源自拉丁的名词并置；density 带后缀 -ity，把形容词 densus 变成可度量的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin densus gives dense, densely, density and densify; populus gives population and populous.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 densus 衍生 dense、densely、density 与 densify；populus 衍生 population 与 populous。

items.example: The noun names a people as a body.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把人民视为整体。

items.example: Population rose along the coast.
The Latin adjective describes close packing.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁形容词描述紧密排布。

items.example: The density of the forest blocks light.
A dense crowd filled the square.
The valley is densely settled.
The plan densifies the inner suburbs.
Population density doubled in a decade.
The delta is densely populated.

definition_zh: n. 口才；雄辩；说服力；意味深长的表达
definition_en: fluent, forceful speech that persuades or moves an audience
core_image: 追悼会上一个人没拿稿子只说了四分钟，讲到一半前排的人低头擦眼睛；壁炉上一张旧照片里父亲的手搭在孩子肩上，谁也没说话；法庭上律师举起一张空椅子的照片
scene: 追悼会上他没有拿稿子，只说了四分钟，讲到一半时前排的人已经低头擦眼睛。 His eloquence held the whole hall silent for four minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 eloquence 指「流畅有力、能说服或打动听众的言辞」（第 1 个义项：口才；雄辩）；句意是他的雄辩让整个大厅安静了四分钟。图中可辨识物件：空着的双手、前排低头的人、手帕。

pos.zh: 口才；雄辩；说服力；意味深长的表达

senses.title: Fluent persuasive speech
senses.definition: fluent, forceful speech that persuades or moves an audience
senses.definitionCN: （名词）流畅有力、能说服或打动听众的言辞
senses.example: His eloquence held the whole hall silent for four minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他的雄辩让整个大厅安静了四分钟。
senses.why: A speaker with empty hands at a lectern while the front row bows their heads.
senses.whyCN: 演讲者两手空空站在讲台前，前排的人低着头。

senses.title: The power to move by words
senses.definition: the quality of expressing feeling so that others feel it too
senses.definitionCN: （名词）把情感表达出来、使他人也感受到的特质
senses.example: The eloquence of her letter made a stranger write back the same week.
senses.exampleCN: 她那封信的感染力，让一个陌生人在同一周回了信。
senses.why: An opened envelope on a doormat beside a reply already stamped and sealed.
senses.whyCN: 门垫上一封拆开的信，旁边一封回信已贴票封口。

senses.title: Expression without words
senses.definition: a look, gesture or silence that speaks as clearly as words
senses.definitionCN: （名词）像言语一样清楚传意的眼神、手势或沉默
senses.example: There was more eloquence in the empty chair than in any speech that day.
senses.exampleCN: 那天空椅子所传达的，比任何一段发言都更意味深长。

intro.en: Eloquence is Latin eloquentia, from eloqui, which joins ex- meaning out to loqui meaning to speak; it is the power of speaking out well.
intro.cn: eloquence 就是拉丁语 eloquentia，来自 eloqui，它把 ex-（向外）与 loqui（说话）结合；它是把话说好的能力。

items.en: Latin loqui means to speak.
items.cn: 拉丁语 loqui 意为说话。

items.en: Adding ex- gives eloqui, to speak out.
items.cn: 加 ex- 构成 eloqui，意为说出来。

items.en: The noun eloquentia names the power of speaking out well.
items.cn: 名词 eloquentia 指把话说好的能力。

items.en: Old French eloquence carried the sense of fluent persuasive speech.
items.cn: 古法语 eloquence 带有流畅而有说服力的言辞之意。

items.en: English took eloquence in the 14C for the art of persuasive speech.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借用 eloquence，指说服性言辞的艺术。

items.en: Writers extended eloquence to looks and silence that speak without words.
items.cn: 作家把 eloquence 扩展到无需言语也能传意的眼神与沉默。

note.en: Eloquence, elocution and loquacious all carry loqui, the Latin root for speak; eloquence persuades, elocution trains the voice, loquacious simply talks a lot.
note.cn: eloquence、elocution 与 loquacious 都带着 loqui，那是拉丁语「说话」的词根；eloquence 说服人，elocution 训练发声，loquacious 只是话多。

dict_mnemonic.text: eloquence ＝ e-（向外）＋ loqu（说话，拉丁 loqui）＋ -ence（名词后缀，表性质）＝「把话说出来的能力」。形容词 eloquent（-ent），副词 eloquently。loqui 这一家按前缀分：e-（外）→ eloquent 雄辩的、elocution 演说术；loquacious 话多的（-acious 爱…的）；soliloquy 独白（solus 独自 ＋ loqui）；colloquial 口语的（col- 一起 ＋ loqui＝一起说话）；ventriloquist 腹语者（venter 肚子 ＋ loqui＝用肚子说话）；circumlocution 迂回说法（circum 绕圈）。注意 eloquence 不只是「说得流利」，fluency 才是流利；eloquence 强调打动与说服。the eloquence of silence 是常见修辞，指沉默比话更有力量。

definition_zh: 基因流；基因流动（通过个体迁移、花粉或种子扩散在群体之间传递等位基因）
definition_en: the transfer of alleles from one population to another through migration, dispersal of seeds or pollen, or human movement
core_image: 山脊隘口的风把一片兰花的花粉吹到另一片兰花上，两种花色在两侧渐渐混匀
scene: 山脊两侧各有一片兰花，花色深浅原本不同，风把花粉送过隘口之后，两边花色的比例渐渐接近。 Pollen carried across the ridge produced gene flow between the two orchid populations.
sceneCN: 这里指群体之间的等位基因传递（第 1 个义项：通过迁移或繁殖体扩散把等位基因带入另一群体）；句意为被风送过山脊的花粉在两个兰花群体之间形成了基因流。图中可辨识物件：山脊、隘口、两片花丛、飘散的花粉。

pos.zh: 名词短语：不可数，指群体间的等位基因传递过程

collocations.zh: 来自野生近缘种的基因流

forms.label: 介词搭配
forms.form: gene flow between A and B

derivatives.zh: 短语的第一个成分，义为「基因」，一九零九年由约翰森定名
短语的中心词，义为「流动」，本指液体的连续移动
同一领域的概念，义为「基因库」，指一个群体携带的全部等位基因
同一领域的量，义为「基因频率」，即某等位基因在群体中的比例
由本短语加「速率」构成，义为「基因流速率」，常以每代迁入个体比例表示

senses.title: The process itself
senses.definition: the movement of alleles between populations when individuals or gametes cross a boundary
senses.definitionCN: 个体或配子跨越边界时等位基因在群体之间的移动
senses.example: Gene flow between the two valleys kept their colour patterns similar.
senses.exampleCN: 两个山谷之间的基因流使它们的花色格局保持相似。
senses.why: A boundary that individuals can cross is also a boundary that genes can cross, so the movement of bodies carries the movement of alleles.
senses.whyCN: 个体能越过的边界，基因也能越过；因此身体的移动同时携带了等位基因的移动。

senses.title: Contrast with genetic drift
senses.definition: a gain of variation from outside, whereas drift is a random loss or fixation inside a closed group
senses.definitionCN: 从外部获得变异，而漂变是在封闭群体内部随机丢失或固定
senses.example: Drift eroded the island's variation while gene flow from the mainland restored it.
senses.exampleCN: 漂变侵蚀了岛上的变异，而来自大陆的基因流又把它补回。
senses.why: Drift only reshuffles what is already present; gene flow is the one force that adds new alleles to a population.
senses.whyCN: 漂变只重排已有的东西；基因流则是唯一能给群体添入新等位基因的力量。

senses.title: Distinction from migration
senses.definition: the genetic consequence of movement, not the movement itself; an individual can migrate without breeding successfully
senses.definitionCN: 移动带来的遗传后果，而非移动本身；个体可以迁移却没有成功繁殖
senses.example: The birds migrated, but gene flow occurred only where they nested and raised chicks.
senses.exampleCN: 候鸟确实迁徙了，但只有它们筑巢育雏的地方才发生基因流。
senses.why: Migration is an ecological event; gene flow is its genetic ledger, and a ledger stays empty when no offspring are produced.
senses.whyCN: 迁移是生态事件，基因流是它的遗传账本；没有产生后代，账本上就是空的。

senses.title: Reducing divergence between populations
senses.definition: the homogenising effect that keeps neighbouring populations genetically similar
senses.definitionCN: 使相邻群体在遗传上保持相似的同质化作用
senses.example: Strong gene flow prevented the two colonies from splitting into distinct subspecies.
senses.exampleCN: 强大的基因流阻止了两个群体分化为不同的亚种。
senses.why: Differences accumulate only when gene flow is weak; constant exchange keeps pulling the two gene pools back together.
senses.whyCN: 只有在基因流微弱时差异才会累积；持续的交换不断把两个基因库拉回同一状态。

senses.title: Barriers and connectivity
senses.definition: geographic features, distance or human construction that reduce the probability of successful exchange
senses.definitionCN: 地形、距离或人造设施降低成功交换概率的情形
senses.example: A new motorway became a barrier to gene flow for the forest frogs.
senses.exampleCN: 新建的高速公路成了林蛙基因流的屏障。
senses.why: Gene flow needs a path; when a barrier makes crossing rare, drift and local selection begin to separate the groups.
senses.whyCN: 基因流需要通路；当屏障使跨越变得罕见，漂变与局部选择就开始把两群分开。

senses.title: Plant-mediated flow
senses.definition: pollen and seed dispersal, which move genes without moving whole plants
senses.definitionCN: 花粉与种子的扩散，在不移动整株植物的情况下搬运基因
senses.example: Wind-borne pollen carried gene flow across the whole meadow.
senses.exampleCN: 风媒花粉把基因流带遍了整片草甸。
senses.why: A plant cannot walk, but its pollen and seeds can travel, so dispersal replaces migration as the vehicle.
senses.whyCN: 植物不会走路，但花粉与种子能旅行，于是扩散取代迁移成为载体。

senses.title: Animal-mediated flow
senses.definition: gene movement carried by migrating herds, birds, fish or insects
senses.definitionCN: 由迁徙的兽群、鸟、鱼或昆虫携带的基因移动
senses.example: Migrating salmon brought gene flow from the sea back to their home streams.
senses.exampleCN: 洄游的鲑鱼把基因流从海洋带回故乡的溪流。
senses.why: Animals that return to breed link distant sites in a single lifetime, making them extremely effective vectors.
senses.whyCN: 返回繁殖地的动物在一个生命周期内就把相距遥远的地点连起来，因此是极高效的载体。

senses.title: Human-mediated flow
senses.titleCN: 人类活动介导的基因流
senses.definition: translocation, stocking, shipping and trade that move organisms far beyond their natural range
senses.definitionCN: 引种、放养、船运与贸易把生物带到远超自然分布范围的地方
senses.example: Ballast water created gene flow between ports that had never exchanged shellfish.
senses.exampleCN: 压舱水在从未交换过贝类的港口之间造成了基因流。
senses.why: Modern transport compresses distance to nearly zero, so gene flow can occur between places with no natural corridor.
senses.whyCN: 现代运输把距离压缩到近乎为零，于是没有天然走廊的地点之间也能发生基因流。

senses.title: Conservation and corridor design
senses.definition: the management use of gene flow to counter inbreeding while avoiding the introduction of maladapted genes
senses.definitionCN: 用基因流缓解近交、同时避免引入不适应当地基因的管理应用
senses.example: Managers allowed limited gene flow to rescue the isolated herd without swamping local adaptation.
senses.exampleCN: 管理者允许有限的基因流来挽救隔离兽群，又不至于淹没本地适应。
senses.why: Too little flow means inbreeding; too much can erase local adaptation, so the useful concept is a controlled rate rather than a maximum.
senses.whyCN: 流得太少会近交，流得太多会抹掉本地适应，因此有用的概念是受控的速率而非越大越好。

intro.en: The phrase pairs a word coined in 1909 for the unit of inheritance with an Old English verb of flowing. Its modern genetic sense belongs to the twentieth century; the exact first printed use of the pair is not fixed.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一九零九年为遗传单位造出的词与一个古英语「流动」动词配在一起。其现代遗传学含义属于二十世纪；两词首次印在一起的准确时间并不确定。

items.en: Genos meant race, stock or kind; Johannsen took it through German to name the gene in 1909.
items.cn: 这个词意为族、种、类；约翰森经德语把它引入，于一九零九年为「基因」命名。

items.en: The new noun named the unit of heredity before anyone knew what it was made of.
items.cn: 这个新名词在人们知道遗传单位由什么构成之前就已为它命名。

items.en: Flowan meant to flow or to run as water does; its noun flow named the continuous movement itself.
items.cn: 这个古英语动词意为像水一样流动；其名词形式指这种连续运动本身。

items.en: Once heredity was counted in populations, the movement of genes between groups needed a name of its own.
items.cn: 当遗传开始在群体中计数，群体之间基因的移动就需要一个自己的名字。

items.en: The fixed phrase spread in the middle of the twentieth century with the rise of population genetics; its first attestation is uncertain in date but not in origin.
items.cn: 这个固定短语随群体遗传学的兴起在二十世纪中叶流行；其首见年代不确定，来源却清楚。

note.en: The first group shares the word gene or the flow frame; the second group names other ways alleles travel or mix.
note.cn: 第一组共享「基因」一词或「流动」框架；第二组是等位基因传播与混合的其他说法。

entries.definition: All the alleles carried by one population at a given time.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻一个群体所携带的全部等位基因。

entries.definition: The proportion of a particular allele within a population.
entries.definitionCN: 某个特定等位基因在群体中所占的比例。

entries.definition: A genetic construct that spreads a trait faster than ordinary inheritance.
entries.definitionCN: 一种让某性状传播得比普通遗传更快的遗传构造。

entries.definition: An informal term for the rate at which genes enter or leave a group.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式说法，指基因进出群体的速率。

entries.definition: A looser wording sometimes used for the same idea.
entries.definitionCN: 有时用于同一含义的较宽松说法。

entries.definition: The ecological movement of individuals, which may or may not carry genes into the breeding pool.
entries.definitionCN: 个体的生态性移动，未必能把基因带入繁殖群体。

entries.definition: The spreading of seeds, spores or young away from the parent.
entries.definitionCN: 种子、孢子或幼体离开亲体向外扩散。

entries.definition: The permanent incorporation of genes from one species into another through hybridisation.
entries.definitionCN: 通过杂交把一个物种的基因永久并入另一个物种。

entries.definition: The mixing of two previously separated gene pools.
entries.definitionCN: 两个先前隔离的基因库发生混合。

entries.definition: Crossing between distinct groups, often the route by which gene flow becomes introgression.
entries.definitionCN: 不同群体间的杂交，常是基因流变成渐渗的途径。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the vehicles of flow; abstract ones treat gene flow as a door in a wall.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着基因流的各种载体展开；抽象联想把它看作墙上的一扇门。

normal.en: Genes travel in bodies, in pollen and in seeds; the traveller is the vehicle.
normal.cn: 基因随身体、花粉与种子旅行；旅行者就是载体。

normal.en: Migration is the walk; gene flow is the birth that follows it.
normal.cn: 迁移是走路，基因流是走路之后发生的繁殖。

normal.en: Drift closes the room, gene flow opens a window.
normal.cn: 漂变关上房间，基因流打开一扇窗。

normal.en: Barriers make flow rare, and rarity lets drift and selection pull the two sides apart.
normal.cn: 屏障让流动变少，稀少又让漂变与选择把两侧拉开。

normal.en: In conservation the useful setting is a controlled trickle, not a flood.
normal.cn: 在保护实践中，有用的设定是受控的细流，而不是洪水。

abstract.en: Gene flow is the only force that adds new letters to a population's alphabet.
abstract.cn: 基因流是唯一能给群体的字母表添入新字母的力量。

abstract.en: A corridor is a sentence spoken between two populations that could not otherwise talk.
abstract.cn: 走廊是两个本无法交谈的群体之间说出的一句话。

abstract.en: Distance is a resistor, and each migrant is a small current.
abstract.cn: 距离是电阻，每个迁入者都是一小股电流。

examples.en: Gene flow from the mainland restored variation the island had lost.
examples.cn: 来自大陆的基因流恢复了岛屿已经丢失的变异。

examples.en: A motorway reduced gene flow between the two frog populations.
examples.cn: 一条高速公路降低了两群林蛙之间的基因流。

examples.en: Pollen dispersal is the main route of gene flow in wind-pollinated grasses.
examples.cn: 花粉扩散是风媒禾草中基因流的主要途径。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「基因 弗楼」——基因像水一样「流」过山谷，把两边的库连起来：基因流

root: 第一个成分由希腊语 genos「族、种」经德语于一九零九年定为「基因」；第二个成分来自古英语 flowan「流动」。整个短语在二十世纪中叶随群体遗传学兴起而通行，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from the bare process to its contrast with drift, its difference from migration, its effects, its vehicles and its management.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从过程本身出发，依次到与漂变的对比、与迁移的区别、效应、各种载体，最后到管理应用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wind over a ridge pass, pollen crossing from one orchid patch to the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：风越过山口，花粉从一片兰花飘到另一片。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: bodies or gametes cross a boundary, and alleles cross with them.
branches.cn: 过程本身：个体或配子越过边界，等位基因随之越界。

branches.en: THE TWO DISTINCTIONS: drift only reshuffles inside, and migration matters only when offspring are produced.
branches.cn: 两组区分：漂变只在内部重排，迁移只有产生后代才有效。

branches.en: THE EFFECT AND ITS BRAKE: exchange homogenises neighbours until a barrier makes crossing rare.
branches.cn: 效应与刹车：交换使邻群同质化，直到屏障让跨越变少。

branches.en: THE VEHICLES: pollen, animals and human transport each carry genes by a different route.
branches.cn: 三类载体：花粉、动物与人类运输各以不同路径搬运基因。

branches.en: THE MANAGEMENT: conservation wants a controlled trickle that fights inbreeding without erasing local adaptation.
branches.cn: 管理应用：保护实践要的是受控细流，既抗近交又不抹掉本地适应。

intro.en: The phrase is two free words; its only bound pieces are the old adjective ending on the first word and the noun endings on both.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个自由词构成；黏着成分只有第一个词上的古老形容词词尾与两个词的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek gives the root for kind or stock; Old English gives the verb of flowing. No Latin noun underlies either half, so the Latin entry list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供「族、种」的词根；古英语提供「流动」动词。两半背后都没有拉丁名词，因此拉丁词条列表留空。

items.example: The root names a line of descent rather than a single trait.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指一条血统，而非单个性状。

items.example: Johannsen created the short form for the unit.
items.exampleCN: 约翰森为这个单位造出这个短词。

items.example: The adjective links the unit to the whole science.
